{

    "src/lib/policy.ts",
    "src/navigation/index.tsx",

    "src/components/ui/MileageCard.tsx",
    "src/lib/mileage.ts",

    "src/screens/AppLockScreen.tsx",

    "src/screens/RestoreScreen.tsx",
    "src/components/ui/BackupButton.tsx",
    "src/components/ui/RestoreButton.tsx",
    "src/App.tsx"
  ],
  "steps": [
    "1. Add the policy text and version to src/lib/policy.ts and make the policy gate store acceptance date/version via the encrypted Store.",
    "2. Extend src/navigation/index.tsx with four bottom‑tab routes: Dashboard, Receipts, Mileage, Settings. Add a stack navigator for modal screens (receipt entry, mileage entry, app‑lock, export, backup/restore).",
    "3. Define core data types (Receipt, MileageEntry, AppSettings) in src/lib/models.ts.",
    "4. Implement a thin domain layer:",
    "   • src/lib/finance.ts – functions to sum income/expenses, compute mileage deduction and estimated tax.",
    "   • src/lib/receiptStore.ts – typed wrappers around getStore() for CRUD on the \"receipts\" collection.",
    "   • src/lib/mileageStore.ts – wrapper for the \"mileage\" collection.",
    "   • src/lib/mileage.ts – mileage‑deduction calculation based on a per‑mile rate from settings.",
    "5. Build the DashboardScreen using shared UI components (Screen, SummaryCard, ReceiptCard, MileageCard, EmptyState). Show total income, expenses, mileage deduction, tax estimate and a list of the most recent records.",
    "6. Create ReceiptsScreen (list) and ReceiptEntryScreen (form). Use FormField, ChoiceField (expense / income) and PrimaryButton. Persist the record via receiptStore.",
    "7. Add a basic SettingsScreen with navigation links to sub‑screens that will be added later (App Lock, Tax Settings, Export, Backup/Restore).",
    "8. Write shared UI components for receipts and mileage cards (ReceiptCard.tsx, MileageCard.tsx) and a generic ExportButton component.",
    "9. Milestone 2 – Photo capture and mileage logging:",
    "   • Add expo-image-picker & expo-file-system usage in src/lib/photoPicker.ts and UI wrapper ReceiptImagePicker.tsx.",
    "   • Extend the Receipt model with optional photoUri (already in models) and modify ReceiptEntryScreen to allow attaching a photo.",
    "   • Implement MileageScreen (list) and MileageEntryScreen (form) using FormField, PrimaryButton and the mileageStore.",
    "   • Create MileageCard UI component.",
    "10. Milestone 3 – Settings, app lock & export:",
    "    • Create src/lib/settings.ts – typed getters/setters for mileageRate, taxRate and appLockEnabled (stored in the Store).",
    "    • Implement src/lib/appLock.ts – thin wrapper around expo‑local‑authentication that can be called from App.tsx after policy acceptance.",
    "    • Modify src/App.tsx to prompt for biometric authentication when appLockEnabled is true.",
    "    • Build sub‑screens: AppLockScreen (toggle), TaxSettingsScreen (inputs for mileageRate & taxRate), ExportScreen (buttons to generate CSV & PDF).",
    "    • Implement CSV export in src/lib/exportCsv.ts (uses fast‑csv‑like string building) and PDF export in src/lib/exportPdf.ts (uses expo‑print to turn simple HTML into a PDF).",
    "    • Wire ExportButton to call the two export helpers and share the file via expo‑sharing.",
    "11. Milestone 4 – Encrypted backup & restore:",
    "    • Write src/lib/backup.ts – serialize all collections, encrypt the JSON blob with a key derived from a user‑provided passphrase (scrypt via src/lib/crypto.ts) and output a Base64‑encoded file.",
    "    • Build BackupScreen (show a PrimaryButton that asks for a passphrase, creates the encrypted blob and invokes expo‑sharing).",
    "    • Build RestoreScreen (prompt for a backup file, ask for the passphrase, decrypt, validate JSON shape, then replace the Store contents via clearAll + bulk put).",
    "    • Add UI buttons BackupButton.tsx and RestoreButton.tsx used in the respective screens.",
    "12. Add required Expo dependencies (expo-image-picker, expo-file-system, expo-sharing, expo-print, expo-local-authentication) via npm install –save‑dev or expo install.",
    "13. Write unit tests for all pure‑logic modules (finance, mileage, backup, settings, appLock) and integration tests that exercise the Store with the in‑memory implementation used by the test harness.",
    "14. Run the template’s existing tests to ensure nothing was broken, then run the newly added acceptance tests for each milestone."
  ],
  "has_ui": true,
  "milestones": [
    {
      "name": "M1: Policy gate, core navigation & receipt entry",
      "goal": "User can accept the policy, navigate the tab bar, add an expense receipt (amount, date, category, type, notes) and see a basic dashboard with total income/expenses. Settings screen shows placeholder links.",
      "files": [
        "src/lib/policy.ts",

        "src/lib/models.ts",
        "src/lib/finance.ts",
        "src/components/ui/ReceiptCard.tsx",
        "src/lib/receiptStore.ts"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "M2: Photo capture & mileage logging",
      "goal": "User can attach a photo to a receipt, add mileage entries (date, miles, purpose) and view them. Mileage deduction is calculated using the default IRS rate.",
      "files": [
        "src/components/ui/ReceiptImagePicker.tsx",
        "src/lib/photoPicker.ts",
        "src/screens/MileageScreen.tsx",
        "src/screens/MileageEntryScreen.tsx",
        "src/components/ui/MileageCard.tsx",
        "src/lib/mileage.ts",
        "src/lib/mileageStore.ts"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "M3: Settings, app lock & export",
      "goal": "User can configure mileage & tax rates, enable optional biometric app lock, and generate CSV/PDF tax‑ready reports that can be shared.",
      "files": [
        "src/screens/AppLockScreen.tsx",
        "src/screens/TaxSettingsScreen.tsx",
        "src/screens/ExportScreen.tsx",
        "src/lib/appLock.ts",
        "src/lib/settings.ts",
        "src/lib/exportCsv.ts",
        "src/lib/exportPdf.ts",
        "src/components/ui/ExportButton.tsx",
        "src/App.tsx"
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "M4: Encrypted backup & restore",
      "goal": "User can create an encrypted backup file protected by a passphrase, share it, and later restore the whole app state from such a file with integrity checks and friendly error messages.",
      "files": [
        "src/lib/backup.ts",
        "src/screens/BackupScreen.tsx",
        "src/screens/RestoreScreen.tsx",
        "src/components/ui/BackupButton.tsx",
        "src/components/ui/RestoreButton.tsx"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

```markdown # DESIGN.md ## Users and goal - **Primary persona**: Freelancers, independent contractors, or gig workers who need to track income, expenses, and mileage for tax reporting without an internet connection. - **Goal**: Record a receipt or mileage entry in ≤ 30 seconds, view an up‑to‑date financial summary, and export or backup data—all while knowing the data never leaves the device. - **Success feels like**: 1. Opening the app shows a clean dashboard with totals instantly. 2. Adding a receipt (or mileage) feels like filling a short form; after saving, a brief “saved” toast appears and the dashboard updates automatically. 3. Exporting a CSV/PDF opens the native share sheet without a loading hiccup. 4. The user can back up data, restore it, and feel confident that nothing is sent to a server. ## Primary flow 1. **Launch** – App checks stored policy version. 2. **Policy gate** (first launch or version change) → user reads the short policy, checks “I agree”, taps **Accept**. 3. **Dashboard** – Shows income, expenses, mileage deduction, estimated tax, and a list of the five most recent entries. 4. **Add entry** – From the dashboard the user taps the **FAB** → selects **Receipt** (or **Mileage**). 5. **Entry form** – User fills required fields, optionally adds a photo (receipt only), and taps **Save**. 6. **Save feedback** – A **Snackbar** says “Receipt saved” (or “Mileage saved”) and the app returns to the dashboard with updated totals. 7. **Optional next actions** – From the dashboard the user can tap **Export**, **Backup**, or **Settings** via the bottom tab bar. *The shortest path to a core job (recording a receipt) therefore consists of steps 1‑6, with no intermediate navigation screens.* ## Screens and states ### 1. PolicyGateScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Loading | Full‑screen ActivityIndicator | “Checking policy version…” | | Agreement (default) | Scrollable text, checkbox, **Accept** button (disabled until checked) | *Policy text* (see Content) | | Error | Full‑screen error view with retry button | “Unable to store your acceptance. Please try again.” | ### 2. DashboardScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Loading | ActivityIndicator centered | – | | Empty | `EmptyState` component | Title: “Nothing here yet”
Description: “Add a receipt or mileage entry to start tracking your finances.”
Primary button: “Add receipt” | | Populated | 4 × `SummaryCard` (Income, Expenses, Mileage deduction, Estimated tax) + recent‑activity list (max 5 items) | – | | Error | Error view with retry | “Failed to load data. Pull down to retry.” | ### 3. ReceiptsScreen (list) | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Loading | ActivityIndicator | – | | Empty | `EmptyState` | Title: “No receipts recorded”
Description: “Tap the + button to add your first receipt.”
Primary button: “Add receipt” | | Loaded | FlatList of `ReceiptCard` | – | | Error | Error view | “Could not fetch receipts. Pull to retry.” | ### 4. ReceiptEntryScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | Form fields (photo picker, amount, date, category, type, notes) + **Save** (disabled) | – | | Validation error (per field) | `HelperText` under the offending field | Specific messages (see Content) | | Saving | Button shows ActivityIndicator, label hidden | – | | Save error | Snackbar | “Unable to save receipt. Please try again.” | ### 5. MileageScreen (list) Same states as **ReceiptsScreen**, with empty‑state title “No mileage logged” and primary button “Add mileage”. ### 6. MileageEntryScreen Mirrors **ReceiptEntryScreen** (no photo field). Validation messages correspond to mileage fields. ### 7. SettingsScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | List of setting rows: App lock (switch), Mileage rate (tap → TaxSettingsScreen), Tax rate (tap → TaxSettingsScreen), Export (tap → ExportScreen), Backup & Restore (tap → BackupScreen), View policy (tap → PolicyScreen), Delete all data (tap → confirmation dialog) | – | | Error | Snackbar | “Unable to load settings.” | ### 8. TaxSettingsScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | Two `FormField`s (Mileage rate, Tax rate) + **Save** button (disabled until changed) | – | | Validation error | `HelperText` under field | “Enter a positive number.” | | Saving | Button shows spinner | – | | Save error | Snackbar | “Failed to save settings.” | ### 9. ExportScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | Two `PrimaryButton`s: “Export CSV”, “Export PDF” | – | | Generating | Full‑screen ActivityIndicator | “Generating export…” | | Share sheet opened | Snackbar | “Export ready to share.” | | Error | Snackbar | “Export failed. Try again.” | ### 10. BackupScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | **Create backup** button | – | | Passphrase modal (default) | Secure `FormField` (passphrase) + confirm field + **Create backup** (disabled until match) | – | | Validation error | `HelperText` | “Passphrases must match and be at least 8 characters.” | | Generating | ActivityIndicator | “Creating encrypted backup…” | | Success | Share sheet + Snackbar | “Backup ready to share.” | | Error | Snackbar | “Backup failed: [reason]” | ### 11. RestoreScreen | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | **Select backup file** button | – | | File chosen → Passphrase modal | Secure `FormField` (passphrase) + **Restore** button | – | | Validation error | `HelperText` | “Enter passphrase.” | | Restoring | ActivityIndicator | “Restoring data…” | | Success | Snackbar | “Data restored successfully.” | | Error | Snackbar | “Invalid passphrase or corrupted file.” | ### 12. DeleteAllDataConfirmation (dialog) | State | UI element | Message | |------|------------|---------| | Default | Dialog with title, description, **Cancel** and **Delete** buttons | Title: “Delete all data?”
Description: “This action cannot be undone.” | | Deleting | ActivityIndicator inside dialog | – | | Success | Snackbar | “All data deleted.” | ## Layout - **Mobile first** – design viewport **390 dp** wide (typical iPhone 12/13). No horizontal scrolling is allowed. - **Global container** – `Screen` component adds `SafeAreaView` + vertical `ScrollView` with **horizontal padding 16 dp** (`spacing * 2`). - **Max content width** – 420 dp (≈ 420 px) for any column; on desktop the column is centered with `margin: auto` and remains 420 dp wide. - **Vertical rhythm** – spacing between stacked elements follows an **8 dp grid** (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32 dp). - **Bottom Tab Bar** – fixed at the bottom, height 56 dp, icons + labels centered. On tablets/desktop the tab bar stays at the bottom to preserve a phone‑first feel; the content column remains centered, never stretched. - **FAB** – anchored to the bottom‑right corner, 16 dp inset from right and bottom edges, size 56 dp (touch target 56 dp × 56 dp). When expanded it shows two **mini‑FABs** (40 dp) for “Receipt” and “Mileage”. - **Cards** – `Card` components have **margin‑bottom 16 dp**, border‑radius 8 dp, elevation 1. We need to consider any potential security issues: injection (SQL etc), broken auth (though no users; just local data and policy acceptance), missing validation, secrets in code, unsafe deserialization, SSRF (not relevant; no network connections except perhaps share sheet), XSS/CSRF (not applicable; mobile app), insecure CORS (maybe web build?), missing rate limiting (not relevant). Since it's a local app that stores data on device encrypted. However, we need to watch for potential issues: using expo-secure-store for key storage is okay. The code writes encrypted data to SQLite. Potential vulnerabilities:

- The policy gate uses a simple boolean to check acceptance; it's irrelevant for security.
- The encrypted store uses AES-256-GCM with random nonce; it's correct. However, there's a potential vulnerability: It uses toBase64/fromBase64 functions that are custom; they might have bug? Possibly but not likely. The algorithm for base64 decoding includes ignoring any non-base64 characters, which may cause padding issues but not security-critical. However, the base64 encoding/decoding doesn't support URL-safe? But it's used for encryption output. It's okay.

- The store's encryption key is stored in secure store, but on web fallback it's stored in localStorage, which is insecure but web is only for checking UI and not production? "web build… used only so the browser checks can walk the UI. localStorage holds ciphertext; the key is kept in localStorage too, so this is NOT a secure store - the real app runs on iOS/Android (device.native.ts)." That's a known insecurity but they mention it's not production. However we need to note that the web build is insecure.

- Any injection attacks? Since the app interacts with SQLite, but the queries are hardcoded and parameterized (execAsync etc). No user-provided strings for SQL queries directly; they use bound parameters for get/insert, no injection.

- Data is stored as encrypted JSON strings; they're parsed with JSON.parse after decrypt. Might be subject to deserialization attacks? If there is malicious data causing prototype pollution? The encrypted data comes from the store originally; if a malicious backup file is imported, it goes through decrypt and JSON.parse for the restored data (in backup?). The backup functionality doesn't appear in code yet. But potential issues: backup file uses deriveKey(passphrase, salt). Not yet implemented; maybe in src/lib/backup.ts but not shown. Even if it exists, JSON.parse is used on decrypted data, but that's representing JSON data for receipt entries and mileage entries; not a risk because it's just data.

- However, there is no explicit validation for user-provided amounts, dates, categories: they are stored as numbers/dates without validation (e.g., amount could be negative? They might accept negative numbers leading to weird totals? It's not a security issue, but might affect accounting.

- There's a potential issue: The PDF export uses expo-print to render HTML with data. If malicious data (like notes) contains HTML or script tags, could cause injection in PDF generation? Expo-print attempts to render HTML; if user includes script or HTML markup in notes or categories, it might be rendered into PDF; but PDF generation on device may not expose attack vector to remote. However, PDF generation may lead to remote script injection if PDF viewer is external; but the PDF is generated locally and not executed on server. Possibly low risk.

- The app includes the ability to share backup file via expo-sharing, which may share encrypted file; but no network connections.

- The code of policy screen includes a readOnly mode for navigation to view policy; but the policy acceptance flow can be circumvented? The navigation includes Policy screen always accessible via navigation (the stack includes PolicyScreen). Since you can navigate to Policy screen at any time (via SettingsScreen's onViewPolicy). That is fine. The policy gate ensures that you can't use other parts unless accepted. But is there any way to bypass? In App.tsx, they check policy on launch, and display Navigation (which includes the PolicyScreen) only if gate is ready. But the SettingsScreen's onViewPolicy means you can navigate to policy screen. However, you cannot navigate to other screens when gate = policy. The Navigation component includes all Tab screens and also policy screen as a separate stack screen; but the app that triggers the gate gating doesn't render Navigation at all before acceptance. So the user cannot navigate to other screens (there is no code for navigation until after acceptance). The policy screen can be accessed only after acceptance, through navigation, but the presence of route may be a risk if there is a direct URL deep link that leads to other screens? Not relevant.

- Info about expo-secure-store: using SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY ensures data is not accessible when device locked; but the app uses optional app lock that can be toggled; but even if user disables it, data is stored encrypted anyway.

1. Nested interactive: FABAdd contains a FAB (main) and mini FABs inside the same container, causing nested interactive elements. According to guidelines, we should not nest pressable inside pressable. The main FAB is a button; mini FABs are also buttons inside the same view. The issue is that the mini FABs appear as children of the main FAB's container (but not inside the main button?). However they are inside same top-level view; but the nested interactive check maybe flags because the mini FABs are within the same view with data-testid="fab-container"? Actually using react-native-paper's FAB may render as button with container class data-testid="fab-container". The mini FABs are separate FAB components but maybe nested because they are rendered as children of the same view that holds the main FAB? The code uses <View> with <FAB> main then conditional <View> containing mini FABs. The main FAB is a button element. The mini FABs are separate button elements, but they are siblings, not nested inside the main button. However the rendered HTML likely nests them due to the FAB's internal structure: the main FAB button may have a container and children? Actually react-native-paper's FAB renders a button element with class fab and maybe includes children? The mini FABs are separate but within the same parent view; still the accessibility tree might treat them as nested because they are inside the same overall container? The error indicates nested-interactive at data-testid="fab-container" for each mini FAB's container. Possibly the main FAB includes an inner container that also includes the mini FABs. To avoid nested interactive, we could separate the main FAB and mini FABs into separate positions: Render mini FABs in their own container not as children of the main FAB element. Perhaps we need to render mini FABs outside of the main FAB component, not inside it. The issue occurs because the mini FABs are placed after the main FAB but maybe the main FAB renders a <button> and the mini FABs render inside the same container? We can instead use two separate FABs at same level, not nested.

Simplify: Instead of having main FAB with mini FABs, maybe we can have separate FABs visible all time: one FAB for adding receipt and one for adding mileage, each with own icon and label, no nested. Remove the toggling main FAB entirely; just show two FABs positioned side by side.

Thus replace FABAdd with two separate FAB components with distinct accessibility labels and no nesting. Provide absolute positioning near bottom right.

Implement new component: FABAdd renders two FABs (or three?) for receipt and mileage, each separate with style bottom offsets.

Also need to remove nested interactive/make open state irrelevant.

2. UI flow step 22: clicks button "Receipt". That expects a button with accessible name "Receipt". Our mini FABs have accessibilityLabel "Receipt". However the test expects to find a button with name "Receipt". If mini FABs are visible directly without needing to open, then test should find them. With open state true they are visible. But they still might be inside container that Chrome's testing sees as nested? Should be fine.

Now check the nested issue: need to ensure not nested: each FAB must not be inside another pressable. Our new component will render two independent FABs within same View container, not nested. That should satisfy.

Implement new FABAdd component accordingly.

Also adjust any imports accordingly.

Let's modify src/components/ui/FABAdd.tsx to replace with two FABs.

Also ensure navigation.getParent()?.navigate('ReceiptEntry') works.

Also we need to adjust any usage maybe not needed.

Proceed to edit file.

We need to fix accessibility color contrast issues for the FAB buttons (Add receipt and Add mileage). The contrast is low because button text color maybe default. In our SimpleAddButtons we used PrimaryButton styled with background secondary etc. But we replaced FABAdd with SimpleAddButtons which are primary buttons, not FAB. Actually in DashboardScreen we now use SimpleAddButtons, which uses PrimaryButton (styled button). The color contrast issue still refers to button text color. Our PrimaryButton default style may be using theme's primary color for text? PrimaryButton uses Button from react-native-paper, mode=contained default uses primary accent color for background and onPrimary for label. But we passed style with backgroundColor: theme.colors.secondary and color: theme.colors.onSecondary but not proper props; PrimaryButton passes style prop, but Button component's style prop sets container style, not text color. Need to set button's mode and contentStyle maybe. However we used PrimaryButton with variant='secondary' which maps to 'outlined' mode. Outlined button uses primary color for border and text; we set style backgroundColor etc but not affecting text color. The color contrast error shows foreground #1d4ed8 (blue) on background #475569 (dark gray) low contrast. Likely the button's text color is primary (#1d4ed8) on secondary background (#475569). That's failing.

Simpler: revert to using FABAdd but ensure button text not needed, only icon. The problem was nested interactive previously caused warnings, we fixed by using Portal for FAB and removed nesting. The color contrast now refers to button's label text, but FAB has no text. In SimpleAddButtons, the PrimaryButton label text is causing contrast. Let's instead implement SimpleAddButtons using FAB but without text, just icons as earlier. However nested interactive was originally because FAB was inside other pressable? Actually original FABAdd placed two FABs directly inside view, inside DashboardScreen which also has other components but not pressable. The nested interactive error maybe because FAB is inside a Pressable? But we changed to Portal which should avoid nesting within other pressables? The issue now is color contrast, not nested. The validator flagged color contrast for buttons (including Fab maybe). Using Portal with FAB icon with custom colors should be fine. But we need to ensure contrast of icon color vs background. The secondary background is theme.colors.secondary (#015958 dark teal) and icon color is theme.colors.onSecondary (#FFFFFF) good contrast. The problem is due to PrimaryButton.

Thus we should remove SimpleAddButtons and revert to using FABAdd with Portal (which we already have) but we still need to ensure no nested interactive: currently FABAdd is rendered inside DashboardScreen directly, not inside a pressable. It's okay. The previous nested errors likely due to other components where FAB was inside Card? Not now.

We set theme colors accent to secondary, which should set FAB background to secondary color. The icon color we set to onSecondary. That should pass contrast.

Thus modify DashboardScreen to import FABAdd (original) and remove SimpleAddButtons import. Also delete SimpleAddButtons file to avoid unused.

# DEPLOYMENT.md

*This guide walks John (or any developer) from the first‑commit version of **apps/freelance-finance-tracker** to a production‑ready iOS/Android release, with optional web fallback. All commands, file names and values are taken from the repository; anything that does not yet exist is marked **TODO**.*

---

## What this app is

- **Type**: Mobile‑first, local‑first finance tracker built with **Expo SDK ?** (the exact SDK version can be obtained with `npm view expo version`).  
- **Core user story**: Users capture receipts (photo + metadata) and mileage logs, see a summary dashboard, and export tax‑ready CSV/PDF files—all stored encrypted on‑device. No network traffic, no analytics, no user accounts.  
- **Key features**:  
  1. Policy‑gate on first launch or when `POLICY_VERSION` changes (`src/lib/policy.ts`).  
  2. Encrypted SQLite store (`src/lib/storage/device.native.ts`) with the key kept in **expo‑secure‑store**.  
  3. Receipt capture (`expo-image-picker`, `expo-file-system`).  
  4. Mileage logging with configurable IRS rate (`src/lib/settings.ts`).  
  5. CSV & PDF export (`src/lib/exportCsv.ts`, `src/lib/exportPdf.ts`).  
  6. Encrypted backup/restore (`src/lib/backup.ts`, `src/lib/crypto.ts`).  
  7. Optional biometric lock (`src/lib/appLock.ts`).  

---

## Architecture

```
+-------------------+      +---------------------+      +-------------------+
|  React Native UI  | ---> |  Lib (finance, …)   | ---> |  Encrypted Store  |
|  (Paper, Nav)    |      |  (pure‑logic only) |      |  (expo‑sqlite)    |
+-------------------+      +---------------------+      +-------------------+
        |                          |                               |
        v                          v                               v
   Expo runtime            Domain layer                     Secure‑Store
   (iOS/Android)            (src/lib/*.ts)            (expo-secure-store)
```

- **UI layer** lives in `src/screens/` and `src/components/ui/`.  
- **Domain layer** (`src/lib/finance.ts`, `src/lib/mileage.ts`, etc.) contains pure functions – fully unit‑testable.  
- **Storage layer** (`src/lib/storage/`) abstracts encrypted SQLite on native and a plain fallback on web (`src/lib/storage/device.web.ts`).  
- **Policy gate** (`src/screens/PolicyScreen.tsx`) checks `POLICY_VERSION` stored via the store.  
- **No backend** – all data never leaves the device.

---

## Prerequisites

| Tool | Version / Install command |
|------|---------------------------|
| **Node.js** | `>= 20` (`node -v`) |
| **npm** | `>= 10` (`npm -v`) |
| **Expo CLI** | `npm i -g expo-cli` |
| **EAS CLI** (Expo Application Services) | `npm i -g eas-cli` |
| **Apple Developer account** | Needed for iOS signing |
| **Google Play Console account** | Needed for Android signing |
| **Java JDK 11+** (for Android builds) | `brew install openjdk@11` (macOS) |
| **Xcode 15+** (macOS) | Required for iOS builds |
| **Git** | `git --version` |
| **Docker** (optional – for web build container) | `docker --version` |

> **NOTE**: The exact Expo SDK version can be queried with `npm view expo version` and should match the version used in `package.json` (the template pins it via `expo install`).

---

## Configuration and secrets

| Item | Where it lives | How to set |
|------|----------------|------------|
| **Expo app config** | `app.json` (already present) | Edit `expo.name`, `expo.slug`, version, etc. |
| **Policy version** | `src/lib/policy.ts` (`export const POLICY_VERSION = "1.0.0"` ) | Bump the constant when the policy text changes. |
| **Encryption key** | `expo-secure-store` (runtime) | No static secret – generated on first launch and persisted by the store. |

## Security checklist

All items stem from **SECURITY.md** findings and from best‑practice hardening for a local‑first Expo app.

- [ ] **Upgrade vulnerable dependencies**

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm test

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
